title: Chat slash-command plane (grammar, aliases, dispatch precedence, unknown-command notice, per-platform command menus)
contract: Any chat message starting with `/` becomes (command, args): `MessageEvent.is_command/get_command` strips a `@BotName` suffix, rejects tokens containing `/` so a pasted path is not a command, and normalises iOS smart dashes so `/model gpt —global` still parses `--global`. Slack threads and Matrix get a per-adapter `!` prefix rewritten to `/` only for known names. One `_COMMAND_LOOKUP` maps 23 aliases to canonical names, and a fixed 18-step dispatch order resolves a typed `/x` against six namespaces (registry → quick → plugin → bundle → skill → unknown notice), with 'registry always wins' so a user command can never shadow `/stop`. Menus are projected per platform: Telegram `setMyCommands`, Slack's 50-slash cap plus `/hermes <sub>`, Discord's 100-command budget. Entries gw-slash.command-grammar / bang-prefix / alias-resolution / dispatch-order / unknown-command / telegram-menu / slack-slashes / discord-skill-slashes / telegramize-mentions, gw-core.unknown-command / telegramize-command-mentions.
governance: The dispatcher itself is read-only routing. Each handler classifies on its own: a handler with an effect must cross its own kernel kind (terminal.exec, repo.sync, goal.approve …); a command must never become a second, unmediated path to an effect the HUD routes through the kernel.

title: Talking to a busy agent: queue / steer / interrupt, `/stop`, and the ack that says what happened
contract: `display.busy_input_mode` picks one of three semantics for a message that arrives mid-turn — redirect the active turn (default), queue it as the next full turn, or steer it into the running turn after the next tool call — with graceful downgrade between them. `/stop` is a hard kill that unlocks the session even if the agent thread is wedged; `/queue` is FIFO; `/steer` appends to the last tool result so role alternation never breaks. A debounced ack tells the user exactly which happened (six distinct strings). Protective demotions: a follow-up cannot interrupt a running subagent or an in-flight compression, near-simultaneous photos batch instead of interrupting once each, and a very fast Telegram follow-up is treated as the same intent. A pending-agent sentinel reserves the slot so a second message cannot spin up a duplicate agent. Every `CommandDef` carries a `busy_policy` of dispatch / reject / interrupt_then_dispatch. ~21 entries incl. gw-core.busy-input-mode / busy-ack / pending-sentinel / subagent-demotion / compression-demotion / photo-burst.
governance: `/stop` and interrupt are privileged control over a running agent, not read-only. Route them through the same origin binding as other operator actions (agents/core/action_origin.py) and record them in the audit chain; stopping a run must be recorded exactly like starting one.
remaining_verbatim: Nerva has one busy-input behaviour: wait for the lease, then reply busy. Hermes has three selectable modes (redirect, queue, steer) and falls back from one to the next when a mode can't apply. Nerva has no /queue or /steer command. /stop does not hard-kill the running model turn or free a wedged session. Only an execute_code child is interrupted.

title: Turn serialization and per-session runtime state (lease, run generations, slot claim, concurrency cap, stale/reaped eviction, warm agent cache)
contract: A turn lease serializes `[load history → run → flush]` per resolved session id (not per routing key). Run generations let a late callback from an abandoned turn detect it no longer owns the session. An active-session slot is claimed before any await, bounded by `max_concurrent_sessions`. Watchdogs evict a session that still claims a running agent but made no progress, and one whose durable routing row was ended while the in-memory slot stayed alive. One `SessionState` object holds all per-session state with three explicit lifetimes; a per-session warm `AIAgent` cache preserves the prompt prefix and is evicted under cgroup memory pressure. ~14 entries incl. gw-core.turn-lease / run-generation / session-slot-claim / agent-cache / agent-cache-pressure / contextvar-reset.
governance: Read-only with respect to the world; but the concurrency cap is a real safety bound — it limits how many kernel-mediated actions can be in flight at once, which the budget layer (agents/core/kernel/budget.py) currently bounds by spend rather than by parallelism.
remaining_verbatim: No run generation lets a late callback from an abandoned turn detect that it no longer owns the session. The only compare-and-set is the checkpoint-clock commit of a compaction (agents/core/orchestrator.py:6440), and it guards a summary, not turn ownership; the H063 route generations in channels/session_lifecycle.py fence which session a channel route resolves to after a reset, not whether a running turn still owns its session. There is no active-session slot claimed before the first await and no `max_concurrent_sessions` cap: turns on different sessions run concurrently without bound (tests/test_turn_lease.py:88). No watchdog evicts a session whose turn is wedged: its lease stays held until the turn ends, and later messages only get the busy reply. There is no eviction of an in-memory slot whose durable routing row ended, and no single per-session `SessionState` object with explicit lifetimes. There is no per-session warm agent cache and no memory-pressure eviction. Agents are process-wide: every session shares `orchestrator.agents`, which the compaction-boundary persona refresh walks as a whole (agents/core/orchestrator.py:601).

title: Pending-input interception (clarify answers, three-way confirm, destructive-command confirm, ephemeral notices)
contract: The gateway holds per-chat pending states and interprets the *next* message as the answer: a clarify question answered by number, by option text, by a comma/space list for multi-select, or free-form prose; a slash-confirm answered by Approve Once / Always Approve / Cancel (native buttons where available, typed keywords everywhere else, `!always` and `!cancel` tolerated); a destructive-command confirm before `/new` `/reset` `/undo` discard history, with a persistent opt-out. `EphemeralReply` renders a system notice that deletes itself so it does not clutter the transcript. 8 entries.
governance: 'Always approve' is a widening of consent and must cross `permission.grant`; a per-chat 'always' that lives only in gateway memory would be an unaudited standing grant.

title: Outbound rendering: streaming edits, tool-progress bubbles, typing/status lines, verbosity tiers

Typing indicators, a text `live_status` line, a long-running 'still working, N min' heartbeat bubble, cleanup of all progress bubbles after the final answer, interim assistant messages, reasoning display styles, an optional runtime footer, configurable status phrases, a 17-language reply catalog, cron output truncation. ~23 entries.

governance: Read-only, but it is an exfiltration control on the same footing as the egress allowlist — the last gate before data leaves the box.

title: Media in and out: inbound attachments, image mode, MEDIA: delivery and the delivery-path allowlist
contract: Inbound: `max_inbound_media_bytes` caps what is downloaded; images are attached natively or pre-analysed into text depending on mode; placeholders and document context notes give the model a textual stand-in; sticker descriptions are vision-captioned once and cached. Outbound: the agent emits `MEDIA:` directives, the gateway auto-appends tags for files it produced and dedups files already delivered in this conversation, delivers them after the text has streamed, and repairs `computer_use_<uuid>` screenshot paths the model rewrote. Crucially, `gateway.strict` + `media_delivery_allow_dirs` + `trust_recent_files` govern **which local file paths the gateway may attach to an outbound chat message**. 10 entries.
governance: Outbound file attachment is egress of local data and must cross the kernel — nearest existing kinds are `channel.reply` (a governed message to a channel) and the `file.write`/`report.export` precedent for leaving the process. It must not be a bare `sendDocument` behind a shape-only contract.

title: Durable delivery ledger and dead-target registry (at-least-once replies)
contract: A durable row per outbound final response in `state.db` with three checkpoints around the send — `pending` before any attempt, `attempting` immediately before the await, `delivered`/`failed` after — plus owner-pid liveness. On startup, rows whose owning process died are claimed and redelivered; after an adapter reconnects without a restart, only an explicit allowlist of transient failures (`send_path_degraded`) may replay. Ambiguity is always labelled, never silently resent: `♻️ Recovered reply — the gateway restarted during delivery, so this may be a duplicate:`. Bounded by MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, 24 h freshness, 7-day retention, 500 rows. A dead-target registry remembers whole-chat `forbidden`/`not found` deaths and self-heals on the next success, deliberately not recording thread-level not-found. 3 entries.
governance: Read-only with respect to the world, but it is the delivery half of the audit guarantee. Redelivery must not re-execute anything — it replays a stored message, never a re-run action.

title: Restart, drain, crash forensics and process supervision
contract: Restart drains in-flight work then respawns through the supervisor or a detached child; affected sessions are notified and offered resume from the last committed turn; a one-shot 'the agent is back' message follows. A drain control marker lets an external process ask a running gateway to stop accepting new turns with no HTTP channel into it. Shutdown flush recovers messages and live transcripts that could not be written to state.db; shutdown forensics records who sent the SIGTERM; a lifecycle ledger records why the previous life ended including SIGKILL and kernel OOM. An in-process daemon thread probes the event loop and hard-exits with the service-restart code after N missed probes; systemd `Type=notify` + WatchdogSec heartbeats only while the loop makes progress. Restart-loop guard, respawn-storm backoff, code-skew detection ('restart the gateway' instead of a cryptic ImportError), cgroup cleanup of orphaned helpers, memory monitor, disk/memory status blocks, readiness probes, startup-restore queueing, a local control socket. ~26 entries.
governance: Restart and drain are privileged host operations. Triggered from chat they must cross `terminal.exec`-class mediation; triggered by the supervisor they are outside the agent's authority entirely and should stay that way.

title: Operator maintenance from chat (`/pause` e-stop, `/platform`, `/restart`, `/update`, `/reload-mcp`, `/reload-skills`, `/debug`, `/diff`, `/egress`, `/version`, `/profile`, plain-text restart coercion)
contract: `/pause [reason|off]` engages or lifts the global emergency stop, and recognised slash commands bypass the pause specifically so a messaging-only operator can always lift it. `/restart` drains and restarts, notifying the requester once back; `/update` launches `hermes update` detached so it survives the restart it causes and streams progress into the chat; a small set of plain-text admin phrases ('restart gateway') is coerced to `/restart` so it never reaches the LLM. `/reload-mcp` reconnects MCP servers and rebuilds the tool set; `/reload-skills` rescans the skills dir and reports the diff. `/debug` uploads a system-info + log-tail report to a paste service and returns links; `/diff` shows fenced git changes; `/egress` reports proxy status, credential source, token mappings and the next remediation step. 13 entries.
governance: `/pause` engage/resume already crosses admin_guard and should also cross `admin.kill_switch`; `/restart` and `/update` are host execution and must cross `terminal.exec` / `repo.sync` (both already registered) with a durable approval — a chat message must never be able to respawn the process directly. `/debug` output must pass row 12's redaction before it leaves the box.

title: Multi-profile gateways, multiplexing, profile routes, relay, peer messaging, hosted rooms and cross-instance handoff
contract: One host can run many profiles as managed services, or opt into a multiplexer where the default profile's gateway serves every profile, with an allowlist; `profile_routes` splits guilds/channels/threads of a *shared* bot token across profiles; `room_link_url` publishes an HTTPS endpoint another gateway may call. Relay mode fronts platforms with an external connector that owns the credentials so the gateway holds no bot token, and can be made the exclusive ingress. `hermes peer` lets bots on one machine message bots on another. Hosted-room workers and a handoff watcher move sessions between instances. ~11 entries.
governance: read-only (nothing to build). Relay in particular would move credentials off the owner's machine, which no kernel kind can compensate for.

title: Scale-to-zero (idle self-suspend of the host)
contract: After `gateway.scale_to_zero.idle_timeout_minutes` of inbound quiet the gateway quiesces its relay link and suspends its own machine. 2 entries.
governance: read-only (nothing to build)
historical_exclusion_reason: This is a hosted-deployment cost feature: it exists so a relay-fronted gateway stops billing VM-hours between messages. Nerva's box is not billed by the hour and is not idle — it runs camera ingestion (agents/core/routers/cameras.py start_camera_ingestion), presence, heartbeats and the night lane of company mode, all of which suspending would silently kill. Shipping it would trade the always-on house brain for a saving the owner does not pay. Re-open path: a laptop-only 'travel profile' with no house role, where suspending is correct behaviour rather than a regression.

title: Gateway configuration surface (layered load order, per-platform shared keys, env overrides, platform enum, port-binding conflicts, cwd/SSL/venv bootstraps)
contract: `load_gateway_config()` merges four layers lowest→highest: dataclass defaults → legacy `gateway.json` → `config.yaml` (with administrator pins applied first) → environment, then validates; a malformed config.yaml logs and continues on the lower layers. Every top-level key is also accepted nested under `gateway:`, with 'key present, not key truthy' precedence. A shared-key loop copies ~30 behaviour keys into each platform's `extra` regardless of nesting; an open enum admits plugin platforms only from bundled dirs or a registry, rejecting arbitrary strings; a single `platform_binds_port` predicate is consulted by both startup validation and the dashboard's pre-write validation so policy cannot drift. ~14 entries incl. the cwd placeholder, Windows venv and SSL bootstraps.

title: The gateway process model itself (one always-on process owning adapters, sessions and the cron tick; the ordered inbound pipeline)
contract: `hermes gateway` runs one long-lived asyncio process that connects every enabled adapter, owns the per-chat session store, runs a 60 s cron tick and dispatches to `AIAgent`; it installs as a systemd user unit or launchd plist, writes pid/lock/state files under `$HERMES_HOME`, and exits 75 to ask for a restart or 78 to mark a permanent config failure so the supervisor stops respawning. The inbound pipeline is an ordered gauntlet every message passes before it can become a turn. ~9 entries incl. the docs pages and package API.
governance: The pipeline is the trust boundary — taint marking here is what lets the kernel later force a plan derived from inbound text back to ASK.
